subject: Proposal: Annual API commit tiers - ACME Systems
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lugo <sara.lugo@acme-sys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Annual API commit tiers - ACME Systems

Sara — great to meet yesterday. As promised, attaching a concise commit proposal aligned to the usage profile you shared (chat-heavy, 30–40 tokens/turn on average). High-level summary below and the attached spreadsheet has the line-item math.

Summary (annual commits, hosted API, per-token pricing):
- Starter: 1,000,000 tokens / year — $0.0015 per token (25% off list)
- Growth: 10,000,000 tokens / year — $0.0009 per token (55% off list)
- Enterprise: 50,000,000 tokens / year — $0.0006 per token (70% off list)

Key behaviors and terms we recommend:
- Monthly smoothing: annual commit divided into 12 monthly invoices to help with budgeting.
- Carryover: up to 10% of unused monthly allocation may roll forward within the contract year.
- Overage: pay-as-you-go at $0.0018/token once the annual commit is exhausted (pro-rated).
- Credits & onboarding: we can add a one-time onboarding credit to offset first-month overages for ramp risk.
- SLA & reporting: 99.9% uptime for hosted API, token-level usage export, and audit logs for compliance.

Attachments: ACME_commit_pricing_v1.xlsx (pricing breakdown), ACME_Draft_SOW_v1.pdf (deployment milestones).

Next steps: If this aligns, I’ll loop in Ben for final discount approval and Marissa for contract/PO flow. Happy to run a short walk-through with your procurement team.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference for production
From: Sara Lugo <sara.lugo@acme-sys.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-sys.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Annual API commit tiers - ACME Systems

Thanks Mina — appreciate the clear breakdown. A few things procurement needs clarified before we can route a PO: 

1) Token counting: do you count prompt+response tokens for usage? We need the exact definition to reconcile with our internal meter.
2) Minimum monthly invoice: can you confirm the minimum billed amount per month under monthly smoothing?
3) Carryover: 10% is reasonable — is that cumulative (e.g., can unused tokens stack to cover future months) or capped per month?
4) SOC 2: please send the SOC 2 report or a secure link and any current pen-test summary.
5) Discount ask: ACME is considering a 2-year commitment; would you consider an additional term discount (or a one-time upfront payment discount)?

Also include a sample contract and the contact for who signs on your side (for electronic signature routing). If we can get answers by Monday, procurement will start the PO intake.

— Sara
Sara Lugo
Senior Procurement Manager, ACME Systems
sara.lugo@acme-sys.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lugo <sara.lugo@acme-sys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Annual API commit tiers - ACME Systems

Sara — thanks, answers below and attaching the draft SOW & contract for PO routing. Quoted excerpts to make reconciliation straightforward.

1) Token counting: we count prompt + model-generated tokens. The usage export includes per-request prompt_tokens and completion_tokens so you can reconcile line-by-line. We can also turn on a detailed export to your S3 on request.

2) Minimum monthly invoice: monthly smoothing means invoice = annual_commit / 12. If actual usage is below the monthly invoice, the remaining tokens are banked up to the 10% carryover cap.

3) Carryover mechanics: unused tokens roll forward and can accumulate within the 10%-of-annual-commit cap (not per-month). For example, Starter's 10% cap = 100,000 tokens total carryover.

4) SOC 2: secure link here: https://redwood.app/secure/SOC2-report (read-only). Pen-test summary attached in the contract appendix.

5) Term discount: Ben is on copy for approvals, but we can offer:
- One-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of the first year invoice to offset ramp risk (applied as invoice credit)
- Additional 5% off the per-token rate for a 2-year committed term on Enterprise tier (requires revenue commit schedule in contract)

Attachments: ACME_Draft_SOW_v1.pdf, ACME_contract_draft_v1.docx

If that looks good, we’ll prepare a countersigned copy once you confirm the tier and PO number. CC’ing Ben to approve the onboarding credit/term discount officially.

LGTM — approve the following for ACME so Mina can finalize the offer: 
- One-time onboarding credit = 10% of year-1 invoice (apply as invoice credit line).
- Optional term discount: for a signed 2-year Enterprise commit, additional 5% off the per-token rate (stackable with Enterprise tier pricing).
- We cannot change carryover beyond 10% without an enterprise legal review.

Mina: you have financial sign-off for these concessions. Keep the contract language explicit about how credits apply (invoice vs. token top-up).

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference

Thanks, Mina and Ben — that works for us. We’ll proceed with the Growth tier (10M tokens) for year 1, apply the 10% onboarding credit, and discuss a 2-year Enterprise evaluation in Q4.

Please send the countersigned contract and a PO template for our finance team. PO will target net-30 payment terms. Procurement contact is procurement@acme-sys.com.

— Sara
